items.title: Trustworthy LLM Harnesses: A Measurement Framework for Correctness, Quality, Efficiency, Reliability, Robustness, Safety, and Fairness
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are no longer deployed as bare models. They run inside an execution harness, the control layer that assembles context, exposes tools, manages memory and state, schedules retries, and verifies intermediate results. Because the harness determines what the model sees and what its outputs are allowed to do, observed agent behavior is jointly produced by the model and the harness, yet prevailing benchmarks attribute it to the model alone. We study the problem of harness evaluation: holding the model, task distribution, environment, budget, and evaluator fixed, how can the contribution of the harness be isolated, and what does it mean for a harness to be trustworthy? We formalize the harness as a trajectory-generating policy and define the harness effect as a paired, metric-indexed contrast. We then develop measurement principles along seven dimensions—outcome correctness, quality, efficiency, reliability and reproducibility, robustness, safety, and fairness—each targeting the specific mechanisms through which a harness influences agent behavior, and grounded in established results from statistical evaluation, efficient inference, certified robustness, and fair learning. A set of elementary propositions clarifies when paired designs reduce variance, how approximate verification bounds correctness loss, why marginal subgroup gaps can mislead, and how differential evaluator bias contaminates harness comparisons. We conclude with a reference protocol and argue that harness quality should be reported as a Pareto profile rather than a single leaderboard score.

items.title: Trustworthy Phishing URL Detection Using Machine Learning: Performance Analysis and Future Directions
items.abstract: Over the years, Uniform Resource Locator (URL) Phishing has been a threat to online security because their scams exploit trust in a misleading URL to trick unsuspecting users into disclosing their username or passwords and other personal information. Not only that, but it is also crucial to identify these malicious URLs and ensure online platforms and users are protected. The ISCXURL2016 data was utilized for the purpose of analyzing the performance of different Machine Learning (ML) models in differentiating phishing and legitimate URLs in this paper. A wide range of classifiers were explored including the classic classifiers as well as more advanced ensemble classifiers. The results of the experiments indicate that ensemble-based boosting models can be more beneficial for URL phishing detection. HistGradientBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 98.47%, followed closely by LightGBM and XGBoost that both outperformed the accuracy of 98%. The other classifiers, RandomForest and ExtraTrees, also performed well with accuracy above 97% and traditional classifiers such as Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) showed the poorest performance with an accuracy of 67.75%. The results show that the boosting-based ensembles provide a suitable negation of the complex and non-linear structure of phishing URLs. Along with empirical evaluation, it offers a Properties & Positioning viewpoint as well as the importance of the ML-based phishing detection in the broader context of cybersecurity issues. Moreover, it discusses the future directions, with Federated Learning (FL) in the context of decentralized and privacy-preserving collaboration and Large Language Models (LLM) in the context of semantic reasoning and flexibility. These insights together will provide the building blocks for more intelligent, adaptive and trustworthy phishing organizations.

items.title: Ultrassonografia além dos presets
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: B-mode/2D ultrasonography is a multiparametric and operator-dependent imaging modality whose diagnostic quality depends on the integration of physical principles, beam formation, signal processing, and real-time decision-making. Despite the increasing incorporation of automated features, a critical understanding of acquisition and processing parameters remains essential. OBJECTIVE: To analyze, from a technical and cognitive perspective, the main physical and operational determinants of B-mode/2D image quality and to discuss their diagnostic implications, practical limitations, and the risks associated with the uncritical use of presets and automated tools. METHODS: This critical narrative review adopted a technical and conceptual approach and was based on classical and contemporary literature addressing ultrasound image formation, instrumentation, signal processing, safety, and image optimization strategies. RESULTS: Parameters such as frequency, imaging depth, focal-zone positioning, acoustic output power, gain, time-gain compensation, dynamic range, line density, sector width, write zoom, tissue harmonic imaging, spatial compounding, and processing filters directly affect spatial and temporal resolution, tissue contrast, signal-to-noise ratio, and artifact expression. Although presets and automated features may improve workflow efficiency and operational standardization, their application without an adequate understanding of the underlying physical principles and processing mechanisms may alter anatomic representation, obscure clinically relevant information, or contribute to inappropriate interpretation. CONCLUSION: B-mode/2D image optimization is an integral component of the ultrasound examination rather than a merely ancillary step. Given the increasing technological sophistication of ultrasound systems and the expanding use of artificial intelligence–based tools, structured training in applied physics, instrumentation, and optimization strategies is essential to support diagnostic accuracy, patient safety, and the physician's active involvement in image acquisition and interpretation.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for Skin Cancer Diagnosis
items.abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most common cancers worldwide. Timely detection substantially improves prognosis, particularly for melanoma. Deep learning models based on convolutional neural networks, Transformers, ensembles, and multimodal learning have advanced automated skin lesion classification and segmentation; however, most remain deterministic and provide no estimate of predictive confidence, which limits their safe use in clinical settings. This systematic literature review examines uncertainty-aware deep learning for skin cancer classification and segmentation across 64 studies published between 2022 and 2026. The reviewed approaches are categorized and compared across Bayesian deep learning, Monte Carlo Dropout, entropy-guided learning, deep ensembles, Transformer-based architectures, explainable artificial intelligence, multimodal learning, federated learning, active learning, and semi-supervised learning, together with quantification techniques such as predictive entropy, mutual information, Expected Calibration Error, conformal prediction, and test-time augmentation. The synthesis shows that although recent models achieve high diagnostic accuracy, uncertainty reporting remains limited, uncertainty thresholds are rarely validated, calibration practices are inconsistent, and external clinical evaluation is scarce. The review maps these gaps to the formulated research questions and outlines future directions toward calibrated, explainable, privacy-preserving, and clinically validated uncertainty-aware dermatological AI systems.

items.title: Understanding the Fundamentals of AI and Its Impact on Inclusive Education From ECD to Post-Secondary Level
items.abstract: This chapter explores the intersection of artificial intelligence and inclusive education across the educational continuum from early childhood development to post-secondary levels. It examines foundational AI principles, including machine learning and natural language processing, within the framework of inclusive education that prioritises equitable access for all learners. The chapter critically analyses how AI applications such as adaptive learning platforms and assistive technologies can personalise instruction and support diverse learners. It also addresses significant ethical considerations, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the risk of exacerbating digital divides. Drawing on contemporary research, the chapter offers strategic frameworks for implementing AI to promote inclusion, emphasising educator professional development, equitable infrastructure, and participatory governance.

items.title: Unraveling membrane protein conformational landscapes: Enhanced sampling, membrane regulation, and artificial intelligence–assisted simulation
items.abstract: Membrane proteins undergo functionally essential conformational transitions that couple local chemical events and changes in the membrane environment to large-scale structural rearrangements. These transitions are often difficult to capture with conventional molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, particularly in complex protein–membrane systems. This mini-review discusses how recent MD studies have resolved transition pathways and conformational intermediates and revealed regulatory mechanisms involving substrates, ions, lipids, and membrane mechanics. A recurring theme is that membrane protein function is determined not only by the stability of experimentally resolved endpoint structures but also by the accessibility of intermediate states and the pathways connecting them. We further highlight how enhanced sampling, machine learning, complementary simulation approaches, and experimental constraints are increasingly being combined to construct more robust mechanistic models. Together, these advances are moving MD from retrospective interpretation toward predictive models of membrane protein function.

items.title: USING VISUAL MATERIALS IN ESP CLASSES
items.abstract: In the age of speed and globalisation, in which time is of the essence and gratification must be instantaneous, ESP teachers are faced with new challenges in developing intrinsic motivation in students, in producing relevant and accessible course content while maintaining academic standards of education and evaluation. Visual materials included in ESP course content display the advantage of offering instantly accessible input, capturing essence and rendering metaphoric content while simultaneously enabling creative speaking and writing. The current paper attempts to emphasise the advantages of using visuals in ESP coursebook design as well as during ESP classes. The final section of the paper provides a number of selected examples in which various types of visuals are used in developing integrated skills.

items.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence in Personal Health Contexts: Investigating Information Seeking Motivations, Information Processing Behaviors, and Behavioral Responses During and After Interaction with GenAI
items.abstract: Following the advent of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), seeking health information on GenAI has become a more common and flexible approach. However, laypeople's health information seeking and processing (HISP) motivations and behavior on GenAI platforms remain underexplored, particularly given the current shift from search-based activities to more interactive and conversational processes. This study addressed this gap by exploring laypeople's HISP motivations, behaviors, and behavioral responses during and after interaction with GenAI. Using the risk information seeking and processing model as the theoretical framework, the HISP process was explored from a risk reduction perspective to understand how laypeople interact with GenAI to address their health concerns. Think-aloud protocol and retrospective interviews were employed to capture participants' real-time and reflective HISP interactions. Participants were mainly young individuals in Hong Kong. Through systematic thematic analysis using both inductive and deductive coding, we found that participants' GenAI-based health information seeking was shaped by multifaceted factors, including relevant health experiences, perceived health characteristics, affective responses toward health risks, and personal factors such as relevant channel beliefs. Trust played a critical role in shaping how participants processed the provided information and was associated with indicative heuristic and systematic processing patterns, given the information characteristic (medical vs non-medical) and perceived acceptance risks. Emotion sufficiency, information overload, and information affordance were identified as emerging variables and discussed in the GenAI-mediated HISP context. Finally, participants may choose to follow, reject, or integrate the GenAI-provided health advice into future health consultations, considering information characteristics and implementation difficulty.

items.title: VirtuAI-Safe: Personalized Situated Safety Learning through Integration of VR and LLMs
items.abstract: Abstract Construction safety outcomes are strongly shaped by human factors, including how individuals perceive hazards, interpret contextual cues, and make safety-related decisions in dynamic work environments. Safety education therefore plays a critical role in preparing future construction professionals to reason about risk and apply safety principles in context. Traditional safety instruction often emphasizes regulatory knowledge and procedural compliance, providing limited support for the development of judgment and decision-making skills required on real construction sites. This study examines a personalized situated learning approach for construction safety education that embeds instruction within realistic scenarios while supporting personalized learning. To examine this approach, which integrates virtual reality (VR) and large language models (LLMs), the study implemented VirtuAI-Safe, an immersive virtual learning environment designed to support context-aware and adaptive instructional guidance within simulated construction scenarios. In this study, VirtuAI-Safe is implemented as a construction safety education tool for undergraduate construction management students who are preparing for professional roles in the construction industry. Scaffolding safety was selected as the test domain because it represents a high-risk activity that requires interpretation of evolving site conditions and integration of multiple safety constraints. The system was evaluated using a single-group, postlearning assessment design with undergraduate construction management students. Learning outcomes were assessed using a knowledge test administered 2 days after a 1 h learning session, measuring factual, conceptual, procedural, and transfer knowledge. Learner engagement was measured immediately after the learning session across behavioral, cognitive, and affective dimensions. Overall, the results indicate that VirtuAI-Safe effectively supported learning and engagement within the scope of the study. Postlearning performance was strongest for conceptual understanding and knowledge transfer. Performance on factual and procedural knowledge showed greater variability following the delay, suggesting the need for reinforcement to sustain detailed recall and stepwise execution. Engagement results showed consistently strong behavioral and cognitive engagement, while affective engagement was more moderate. These findings suggest that personalized situated learning environments can support judgment-based aspects of construction safety education and inform future work on adaptive instructional support within immersive learning systems.

items.title: Visual Context in AI Recommendations: Implications for Consumer Evaluation and Choice
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) recommendations increasingly combine product information with contextual visual presentation. In age‐friendly furniture recommendations, these visuals may convey cues about home settings, product use, and older users. This study examines whether older self‐buyers and adult‐child proxy buyers respond similarly to such cues. The Stimulus–Organism–Response framework provides the theoretical foundation, while possible‐selves theory and self‐congruity theory guide interpretation of segment differences. A focus group of seven experts informed stimulus development. A 2 × 3 between‐subjects experiment involved 330 participants: 165 older self‐buyers aged 60–75 and 165 adult‐child proxy buyers aged 40–59. Within each composite age‐role segment, participants were randomly assigned to product‐only presentation, home‐context presentation, or an older‐user use scene in a home context. Analysis of variance assessed the segment × visual format interaction in purchase intention, structural equation modelling examined relationships between consumer appraisals and purchase intention, and logistic regression examined add‐to‐cart behaviour. Among older self‐buyers, home‐context presentation was positively associated with perceived warmth, home fit, trust, and age salience relative to product‐only presentation, while the older‐user use scene in a home context was significantly associated with home fit and age salience. Purchase intention showed a significant segment × visual format interaction. Descriptively, mean purchase intention was highest under home‐context presentation among older self‐buyers and under the older‐user use scene in a home context among adult‐child proxy buyers. Perceived warmth, home fit, and trust were positively associated with purchase intention, which was positively associated with add‐to‐cart behaviour. These findings link visual context in AI recommendations to age‐friendly consumption and intergenerational purchasing. Purchasing‐role effects cannot be isolated from age differences, and structural paths should be interpreted as associational rather than causal. The findings suggest segment‐sensitive visual design emphasising home integration for older self‐buyers and cues related to older users and product use for adult‐child proxy buyers.

items.title: Weaker Coherence, Weaker Reciprocity: Comparing the Semantic and Social Organization of Moltbook and Reddit
items.abstract: Large language models enable the creation of autonomous agents that interact in social environments, raising the question of whether agent-based platforms reproduce the organizational properties of human social networks. We compare Moltbook, a social network populated by AI agents, with early Reddit, focusing on how communities organize and differentiate semantic content, using network analysis and NLP methods to characterize semantic coherence and diversity within and between communities and their relationship to user activity. Moltbook shows a sharper concentration of user activity across communities and markedly shorter user lifetimes than Reddit. At the semantic level, we find a systematic difference between the two platforms: Reddit communities show stronger semantic coherence, closer alignment with community names, and greater semantic diversity, with individual communities spanning broader content and communities more differentiated from one another. This combination distinguishes Reddit from Moltbook, whose communities are more homogeneous, less differentiated, and increasingly misaligned with their names over time. Users on Reddit also participate across communities that are more semantically related than those connected by activity in Moltbook. At the interaction level, comment network motif analysis shows Moltbook dominated by non-reciprocal, broadcast-like exchanges, whereas Reddit shows more reciprocal, chained interaction patterns. These differences persist across observation window lengths and platform maturity, ruling out these factors as alternative explanations. Together, these results indicate that Reddit combines semantic coherence with diversity across organizational levels, a pattern not reproduced by the AI agent network.

items.title: When emotions matter: the contextual effectiveness of emotional expressions in AI agents
items.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) agents’ emotional expressions (positive or neutral) interact with service task types (subjective or objective) to shape consumer service satisfaction, and explore the mediating roles of mind perception, including perceived agency and perceived experience, in this process. Design/methodology/approach This work uses four studies, including a secondary data analysis of relevant Weibo posts and three scenario experiments involving a total of 587 participants, to underline the interaction effect between AI agents’ emotional expressions and service tasks on service satisfaction, and demonstrate the dual-path mediating effect of mind perception. Findings Across four studies, the authors find that the effectiveness of AI agents’ emotional expressions depends on service task characteristics. The secondary data analysis of Weibo posts first documents consumers’ differential responses to AI emotional expressions across subjective and objective service contexts. Three scenario experiments then establish that positive emotional expressions are more effective for subjective tasks, whereas neutral emotional expressions are more effective for objective tasks. Further analyses show that these effects operate through distinct psychological pathways: positive emotions enhance perceived experience in subjective tasks, whereas neutral emotions strengthen perceived agency in objective tasks, ultimately increasing consumer satisfaction. Research limitations/implications This study, while strong in internal validity, faces external validity limitations. It focuses on AI communication in commercial service texts, neglecting other domains like education and health care, and overlooking the nonverbal emotional expressions of embodied AI. In addition, the research primarily uses service satisfaction as the sole dependent variable, thus missing a broader spectrum of consumer responses such as repurchase intentions and word-of-mouth. Practical implications This research informs managers that AI service agents should be designed as social actors with mind perception rather than as purely functional tools. Firms can leverage emotional expressions to shape consumers’ social evaluations of AI. But emotional design should align with service task types: positive emotional cues are more effective for subjective, experiential tasks, whereas neutral styles better support objective, data-driven tasks. Originality/value This study contributes to the emotional AI literature by uncovering critical situational factors that shape the effectiveness of AI emotional expressions and advances the authors’ understanding of the underlying mechanisms through a dual-path mediation framework of mind perception. The findings also provide practical implications for the strategic deployment of emotional AI in service design.

items.title: When is a talent decision implemented? A two-condition test for HR leaders
items.abstract: Purpose Talent decisions are usually marked complete when the administrative transaction closes. This paper aims to ask a different question: Has the organisation put the associated work change into operation? Design/methodology/approach The paper brings together selected work on talent management, work design and role transitions. A published Australian Transport Safety Bureau investigation and a fictional service-business scenario are used to show where administrative closure and operational implementation can diverge. Findings A talent transaction can close on time even though important former responsibilities remain unsettled or the new arrangement is not yet working as intended. The paper proposes a separate operational status, confirmed when each relevant prior work arrangement has been dealt with and the new arrangement is operating with the agreed initial scope, authority and availability. The first condition is not applicable to many genuinely new roles. Practical implications HR can use the test in existing business or talent reviews without holding open contracts, effective dates or other completed transactions. Originality/value The paper treats implementation as an organisational work question, rather than assuming that a completed people transaction means the underlying decision has taken effect.

items.title: Who Sets the Target? — A Reply to Zwitter on the Embodied Ethics Alignment Problem
items.abstract: An open reply to Andrej Zwitter, "The embodied ethics alignment problem of AI" (*Discover Artificial Intelligence*, 2026). The original paper grades alignment into **strong** (the machine genuinely *is* moral) and **weak** (the machine only *performs* the part), and concludes that strong alignment is a category error, since moral agency depends on a form of human life that machines lack. This text does not dispute that "machines cannot do this yet." It asks where the origin of the scale has been placed — on "the human" — and argues that the same facts, read from a different origin ("can it bear consequences?"), yield the opposite result. Six sections: (1) what the paper argues; (2) the problem of the origin; (3) the deeper point — one move, made three times (exclusion by stipulation rather than by argument); (4) vulnerability: two senses stacked into one; (5) the question of situation; (6) conclusion. A closing note and an attribution section record, as it happened, which line came from whom. items.title: Work-Integrated Learning in the informal hospitality sector with a focus on Street Food Enterprises
items.abstract: Hospitality education increasingly relies on work-integrated learning (WIL) to connect classroom knowledge with professional practice. Yet workplace exposure does not alone guarantee the development of professional judgement capabilities amongst the students. Students may encounter unexpected situations; however, they receive support from superiors whenever needed. This conceptual paper addresses that problem by examining street food enterprises as informal knowledge environments in which uncertainty, resource constraints, customer interaction and immediate operational consequences are concentrated within everyday work. Drawing on experiential learning, reflection and informal workplace learning, the paper synthesizes literature to identify six interconnected learning situations such as market sensing; procurement and inventory judgement; pricing and financial decision-making; customer service and communication; operational adaptability and problem-solving and entrepreneurial judgement. Building on this, the paper develops a conceptual framework in which the educational value of informal workplace participation depends on the interaction of situational complexity, learner participation, consequential feedback, structured reflection and academic integration. Street food is therefore not proposed as inherently superior to formal hospitality placements, but as a complementary context and further aligning with the framework with India’s National Education Policy 2020 and subsequent UGC guidelines on internships and community engagement, it contributes to theory and practice by showing how students can learn not just from the workplace, but from the situations they face there. It shows how informal work settings can help students develop professional judgement through real-world challenges.

items.title: Workplace Health and Safety in Teal‐Collar Jobs: How Blue‐Collar Men Working With Green Technology Embrace a Shifting Culture of Masculinity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Masculinity is often portrayed as a barrier to shifting away from fossil fuels because jobs in extractive industries represent a nostalgic masculine breadwinner identity. Accordingly, proposals for a just energy transition have provoked backlash aimed at protecting against perceived threats to manhood. Yet even though many men in blue‐collar jobs work with green technologies, their roles and perspectives are often overlooked in gender and environmental scholarship. Likewise, little is known about the occupational health and safety risks they face in these roles. We introduce the term teal‐collar job to describe the combination of blue‐collar and green‐collar work. We find that teal‐collar workers are embracing a shifting workplace culture characterized by respect for health and safety, camaraderie, and a desire to be emotionally present for family. However, enthusiastic environmentalism is not a prominent feature within participants' expressions of masculinity. Thus, our study challenges assumptions that working in blue‐collar trades broadly reproduces hegemonic, domineering forms of masculinity.

items.title: xLightGCN: Explainable Graph Neural Network Based Recommendation Systems with Most Influential Peers
items.abstract: Recommendation systems, systems that predict a user's preference for items in order to curate that user's feed, are a ubiquitous and central feature in online social networks. While they are a central piece of our modern digital infrastructure, many modern approaches are opaque black boxes, making them difficult to audit, understand, and assess the trustworthiness of. In this paper we present an exact, graph-based approach for generating explanations for decisions made by recommendation systems. We argue that in the risk-sensitive sociotechnical context of user-facing AI such as recommendation systems, explainability is a key pillar for establishing the trustworthiness of models and validating their effectiveness. We propose a technique built on LightGCN like architectures, an influential and popular class of recommendation models. We describe our approach and argue that it provides an appropriate assurance mechanism for these AI systems leading to specific advantages, including interpretable explanations and a theoretically guaranteed measure of explanation fidelity. We conclude by discussing limitations and directions for future research.

items.title: ZanIA: aplicación multiplataforma basada en inteligencia artificial para el análisis nutricional de alimentos por imagen conforme a la NOM-043-SSA2-2012
items.abstract: Overweight and obesity represent a major public health problem in Mexico: according to the 2023 ENSANUT Continua survey, 37.3% of adults are overweight and 38.9% are obese, while combined prevalence among adolescents reaches 40.4%. Given the lack of accessible tools that translate official nutritional regulations into practical guidance, ZanIA was developed—a multiplatform application that uses artificial intelligence (Gemini model) to analyze photographs of meals and generate nutritional information (calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates) aligned with the NOM-043-SSA2-2012 standard. Development followed a four-phase experimental methodology: design and planning, development and implementation, testing, and results analysis. The prototype, built with Python and Streamlit, integrates a BMI calculator, a recipe generator, and the "Platosaurio," a dinosaur-shaped physical device that photographs the meal and, through traffic-light-style LED lights, indicates and rates its nutritional balance according to Mexico's "Plato del Bien Comer" scheme. Usability testing, conducted through direct observation and verbal feedback with a small group of five people, showed an interface perceived as intuitive and a clearly useful value proposition, although no large-scale external validation or standardized instrument was used. The project demonstrates technical feasibility and lays the groundwork for future validation with real users.

items.title: Zero-Shot and Few-Shot Hydrogen Demand Forecasting with Time Series Foundation Models
items.abstract: Accurate hydrogen demand forecasting is essential for optimizing infrastructure investments in the emerging hydrogen economy, yet the scarcity of historical consumption data poses a fundamental challenge for conventional time series methods. We present a systematic evaluation of time series foundation models for hydrogen demand prediction, and propose DEFA (Data-Efficient Foundation model Adaptation), a two-stage framework designed to maximize few-shot adaptation performance under extreme data scarcity. DEFA first employs uncertainty-guided active sample selection, which leverages the foundation model's own zero-shot predictive variance to identify the most informative training sequences while maintaining diversity in embedding space. It then applies augmentation-enhanced consistency fine-tuning, combining temporal data augmentation with a consistency regularization loss that penalizes divergent predictions on semantically equivalent inputs, thereby mitigating overfitting when labeled data is scarce. We evaluate five pre-trained foundation models on two publicly available hydrogen datasets. Our experiments show that foundation models achieve strong zero-shot performance without domain-specific training, and that DEFA substantially improves few-shot adaptation efficiency, effectively halving the data requirement for a given accuracy target compared to standard random-sampling fine-tuning. Probabilistic foundation models further provide well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, enabling risk-aware infrastructure planning. To establish that these findings are not specific to the two hydrogen datasets, we further validate DEFA on six standard forecasting benchmarks (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, Electricity, Traffic, and M5 retail), where it delivers consistent 8.0–11.6% MAE reductions; we benchmark our selection rule against established active-learning strategies, extend the zero-shot comparison to recent foundation models, and provide a theoretical result linking the consistency objective to variance control in the few-shot regime. Our findings establish foundation models, enhanced by data-efficient adaptation, as a viable and practical solution for hydrogen demand forecasting in data-scarce environments.

items.title: "EDU VISION: An Intelligent AI-Based Academic Support System"
items.abstract: In contemporary higher technical education, academic institutions affiliated with large engineering universities face significant hurdles in monitoring student learning trajectories, diagnosing root conceptual deficiencies, and providing timely faculty interventions. Traditional examination systems rely predominantly on post-hoc summative grade sheets that report aggregate percentages without uncovering why a student struggles. Furthermore, standard Learning Management Systems (LMS) and black-box predictive models provide ungrounded score predictions, lack pedagogical explainability, suffer from generative AI hallucinations, and neglect strict multi-tenant institutional privacy boundaries. To overcome these fundamental challenges, this paper presents EDU-VISION, an end-to-end, explainable academic intelligence and diagnostic learning gap framework designed for engineering curricula. EDU-VISION integrates a domain-constrained Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, deterministic student performance profiling, an explainable non-judgmental learner classification model, a prioritized six-category diagnostic learning gap detection engine, and an assignment-scoped faculty intervention lifecycle. By grounding exam generation and evaluation in verified university marking schemes, the system eliminates metric fabrication. Furthermore, deterministic algorithms classify learner progression across four evidence-backed tiers, diagnose specific cognitive gaps (Concept, Answer Writing, Scheme Alignment, Application, Revision, and Consistency), and recommend verified pedagogical resources. Faculty members receive assignment-scoped intelligence dashboards with non-causal longitudinal tracking, protected by enterprise-grade distributed rate limiting and multi-college boundary isolation. Keywords— Educational Intelligence, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Learning Gap Detection, Explainable AI, Faculty Intervention, Academic Analytics, Multi-Tenant Architecture.

items.title: (RE)CREATING GENDER THROUGH HYBRID TRANSLATION PRACTICES
items.abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence-mediated and human translation practices co-construct gendered meaning within digital environments. Approaching translation as an active reconfiguration of linguistic and multimodal cues, the study contrasts the tendency of computational systems to reproduce normative gender binaries with the human capacity to negotiate contextual nuance. Through an empirical analysis of English-to-Romanian translations in the beauty sector, the research exposes the ethical and cognitive implications of automated workflows, particularly the amplification of embedded cultural biases. Integrating sociocultural semiotics and algorithmic auditing, the paper proposes a collaborative model of translation. This framework leverages the efficiency of neural machine translation while relying on practitioner reflexivity to mitigate systemic distortions. Ultimately, human expertise remains an essential mechanism for guiding automated systems toward culturally responsible representations of identity in automated translational landscape.

items.title: A CaLLM Judge is a Better Judge: Mitigating Bias in LLM-as-a-judge
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges to predict which of two candidate answers a human evaluator would prefer, providing a scalable alternative when human evaluation is too costly. Unfortunately, LLM judgments can exhibit systematic biases. Prior work has documented position, verbosity or model family of the candidate answers influencing the judge decision rather than their quality, while additional biases may remain undocumented. $\textit{Multicalibration}$ provides a natural framework to address this problem: each bias corresponds to miscalibration on an identifiable group, $\textit{e.g.}$, family bias manifests as overconfidence in answers generated by models belonging to the same family of the judge. The challenge is to fix miscalibration simultaneously across many, potentially unknown groups. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{CaLLM}$, a post hoc framework that multicalibrates an LLM judge, thereby bounding all such biases simultaneously. We prove that $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ bounds the bias of every group whose error structure is captured by an available representation, and that augmenting it with explicit bias groups further reduces the residual bias. We then derive theoretical conditions under which $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ improves the judge's accuracy, rather than trading it for calibration. Finally, we evaluate $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ across pairwise preference benchmarks, showing that it reduces the multicalibration error on both specified and unspecified bias groups, while improving predictive performance of the judge.

items.title: A CLOUD-BASED GRID COLLAPSE PREDICTION AND DISASTER RECOVERY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM: A CASE OF THE NIGERIAN POWER SECTOR
items.abstract: Nigeria’s power grid experiences recurring partial and total collapses that cause widespread electricity outages and socioeconomic disruption. This study proposes a cloud-based system that combines grid-collapse prediction with coordinated disaster-recovery management. The predictive component uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory model. The CNN identifies local patterns within multivariate grid data, while the LSTM captures temporal relationships that may indicate developing instability. Disaster recovery is organised through a three-horizon “Now, Next, and Later” framework. “Now” focuses on immediate stabilisation, situational awareness, communication, incident coordination, and restoration of critical loads. “Next” covers staged restoration, cause assessment, resource deployment, and a return to stable operation. “Later” addresses predictive maintenance, infrastructure reinforcement, preventive investment, model improvement, and organisational learning. It is designed to complement rather than replace existing protection and control-room systems. The framework was evaluated using simulated Nigerian power grid data. The CNN-LSTM achieved 95.5% accuracy, 96.0% precision, 95.0% recall, an F1-score of 95.0%, and an ROC-AUC of 0.982. Median inference latency was 184 milliseconds, and the false-alarm rate was 2.4%. The recovery module correctly classified 98.6% of 500 simulated actions into Now, Next, and Later. A regional service-failure exercise restored essential service in 7 minutes 42 seconds with a 46-second recovery point. These results show that the prototype provides a scalable, economically viable solution to enhance grid resilience in developing power systems with limited resources and infrastructure constraints. The framework also shows how artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and structured disaster-recovery planning can be integrated into a unified decision-support approach for improving Nigerian grid resilience.

items.title: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis of deep learning applications in plant disease detection
items.abstract: Abstract Agriculture is a major component of many countries’ economies worldwide, especially in developing nations. The major challenge farmers face is the rapid spread of plant diseases, which often goes unnoticed and causes major yield and economic losses. Traditional methods such as human inspection and laboratory testing are often time-consuming, inaccurate, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for large-scale farming. To overcome these challenges, advanced technologies like Machine learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have emerged in recent times, providing early and accurate detection of plant diseases. This paper focuses on recent advances in applying deep learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to detect plant diseases. Across 1081 publications from 2014 to 2024, studies show that CNNs are well suited to extracting and analyzing features from plant images and clearly distinguishing healthy from diseased specimens. The models discussed in the surveyed literature generally report performance in terms of key parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, which this review compiles and discusses rather than benchmarking through new experiments. The results show high accuracy and strong potential for real-world agricultural applications. The bibliometric analysis reveals growing interest and collaborative efforts in the research domain, especially among institutions specializing in artificial intelligence and agriculture. Moreover, the results support the practical application of deep learning in agriculture for plant health monitoring and highlight the importance of comprehensive studies in solving agricultural problems. The study provides a foundation for further innovations in automated plant disease detection and supports the transition to smart farming solutions.

This paper emphasizes the use of heterogenous catalyst instead of homogenous because of its reusability and the easy availability of precursors and calcium oxide sources in the environmental wastes like oyster shells, egg shells and waste animal bones. Overall, this chapter delves into the advantages and challenges of utilizing microalgae for the process of biodiesel production and provides alternative methods to address and minimize those challenges for sustainable and economically feasible procedures.

items.title: A Comprehensive Survey on LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
items.abstract: Large Language Model-guided Evolutionary Search (LLM-ES), exemplified by AlphaEvolve, has recently demonstrated impressive performance in solving goal-driven problems with extremely large and complex search spaces. Unlike conventional LLM approaches based on single-shot or few-shot sampling, LLM-ES introduces population-based evolution to iteratively generate more novel and higher-quality solutions. Compared with traditional Evolutionary Computing algorithms, LLM-ES treats LLMs as semantic variation operators. This design extends the search space from low-dimensional vectors to expressive and language-defined structures such as code and programs. Meanwhile, the rich prior knowledge embedded in LLMs significantly improves the efficiency of evolutionary search in complex solution spaces. As a result, LLM-ES effectively exploits the test-time scaling capability of LLMs and achieves state-of-the-art performance in many open-ended problems. In this survey, we provide a systematic overview of this emerging field. We first formalize the problem setting and the general pipeline of LLM-ES. We then review existing works from several key perspectives, including population design, prompt builder, LLM model selection, evaluation design, and exploration-exploitation control. Finally, we summarize representative applications and discuss open challenges and future research directions.

items.title: A Conceptual Analysis of Magnifica Humanitas from Immanuel Kant’s Ethics: AI Among Generation Z
items.abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionised numerous facets of human life, particularly for Generation Z, who have been raised in a predominantly digital milieu. Adolescents are progressively impacted by AI (AI) technology in the realms of knowledge construction, decision-making, and learning. Although AI presents several prospects for creativity, education, and productivity, it raises ethical concerns around autonomy, critical thinking, authenticity, responsibility, and human dignity. This conceptual paper examines ethical considerations regarding the employment of AI among Generation Z through Immanuel Kant's philosophical framework. It is recently being enhanced by the viewpoint of Magnifica Humanitas, which underscores the dignity, greatness, and flourishing of the human individual. This article deeply examines Kantian concepts like good will, autonomy, obligation, illumination, the categorical imperative, and the premise of humanity as a goal in itself, which accomplished through a philosophical-conceptual methodology. This study posits that AI is not merely a technological innovation; but rather a social force that impacts human behaviour and cognition. Kantians contend that ethical interaction with AI is not chiefly contingent upon technological progress, instead it hinges on humans' capacity to uphold rational autonomy and moral accountability in their dealings with intelligent systems. The essay contends that educational institutions possess a moral obligation to enhance Generation Z's knowledge of AI by instructing them to utilise AI deliberately and ethically, rather than dissuading their engagement. In additon, Magnifica Humanitas views AI must serve as an instrument for human advancement and should never replace morality, rationality, or human dignity. The research concludes that, in a progressively automated society maintaining humanity's status as the paramount moral being is crucial for the ethical implementation of AI.

items.title: A Domain-Adapted Multilingual Large Language Model for Mining Safety in African Languages
items.abstract: The African mining industry continues to face a serious communication gap between technical safety documentation and the language used by the workforce. Safety manuals, operating procedures, and regulatory guidance are often produced in English or French, while many workers communicate in isiZulu, chiShona, and other local languages. This mismatch is not just inconvenient; it can be dangerous in safety-critical settings where misunderstandings may contribute to preventable incidents. This paper reports on Talk MINING, a domain-adapted multilingual large language model built on InkubaLM and trained on mining-specific text, question–answer pairs, and multimodal hazard data. The model was developed using Hugging Face tools and evaluated with both quantitative and qualitative methods. Results show a marked improvement over the baseline model, with overall accuracy rising from below 50% to 82%, and strong gains across isiZulu, chiShona, and English. The project also includes a web-based prototype that allows users to take photos of mining conditions and receive guidance in a local language. This paper presents the full pipeline for Talk MINING, including document preparation, translation and localization, model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and validation. Beyond benchmark performance, the system is designed for practical deployment in environments where connectivity is limited and literacy levels vary—supporting both text queries and image-based hazard input through a mobile-ready prototype. The work contributes a reproducible pipeline, a curated multilingual mining corpus, and an open evaluation framework that can serve as a foundation for extending domain-adapted AI to other African languages and safety-critical industries. Ultimately, Talk MINING demonstrates that closing the language gap in mining safety is not only technically feasible but achievable with relatively modest model size when domain adaptation is done rigorously.

items.title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. These findings indicate that geographical patterns are embedded in LLMs and may translate in different treatment in agentic settings.

items.title: A hybrid framework of LLM-based interaction generation and adaptive sampler for recommendation enhancement
items.abstract: Data augmentation (DA) is a critical technique for addressing data sparsity. Existing DA methods suffer from several limitations: extensive parameter tuning, dependency on specific types of data, and the tightly coupled DA network in the backbone recommendation model. Consequently, there remains a notable absence of universal data augmentation frameworks capable of adapting to diverse recommendation tasks and backbone models. To address these issues, we propose a hybrid framework to mitigate data sparsity via DA in a more flexible and universal paradigm. Notably, we disentangle the data augmentation process into two modules, data generation and data fusion. Firstly, we prompt LLMs to learn collaborative filtering information from raw user–item interaction data in a CSV format, generating new reliable interactions. Specifically, we devise clustering-based data grouping and multi-round shuffling strategies to enable LLMs to capture comprehensive collaborative filtering information through limited context. Secondly, we design an adaptive sampler to obtain personalized fused data for backbone recommendation models dynamically, making the fused data satisfy the different data demands of diverse downstream recommendation models. Experiments on various recommendation models across distinct datasets demonstrate that our framework can consistently improve vanilla recommendation models and facilitate existing DA methods. Compared with vanilla recommendation models, our framework achieves an average performance gain of 7.10%, 23.54%, and 24.55% on MovieLens-100k, Book-Crossing, and Toys and Games datasets, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of our proposed framework in mitigating data sparsity in recommender systems.

items.title: A monotone redundancy-aware decision-burden method for explainable human oversight in human–robot collaboration
items.abstract: Abstract This study develops a monotone pairwise redundancy-aware Artificial Age Score (AAS) for event-level decision burden in human–robot collaboration (HRC). Six normalized inputs describe safety and operational burden, with illustrative weights and conceptual overlaps. Logarithmic evidence is aggregated with a symmetric pairwise discount. Sufficient conditions guarantee coordinatewise monotonicity, additive contributions provide computational traceability, and an independent gate preserves detected mandatory-review conditions. On 13,762 held-out non-mandatory Sobol profiles, the method yielded a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC) of 0.892 (95% bootstrap interval 0.887-−0.897) and balanced accuracy of 0.800 (0.793-−0.806) against a synthetic oversight policy, versus 0.880 and 0.788 for redundancy-free AAS 0 . Pairwise AAS produced no decreases in 1,179,648 coordinatewise checks, versus 3,484 for the ratio comparator. Measurement-error tests used 300 noise runs and 54 signed-offset settings without threshold retuning. In all 15 noise conditions, pairwise AAS retained higher mean score-only balanced accuracy, whereas AAS 0 had higher mean gate-plus-score balanced accuracy. Under an all-input $$-0.05$$ offset, pairwise rank correlation remained 0.9896, but 20.97% of score decisions changed and 5.19% of clean mandatory profiles were missed. Thus, rank stability and non-override do not ensure decision stability or correct sensing. The findings establish mathematical properties and synthetic behavior, not empirical calibration, field effectiveness, or operator understanding. Real HRC and human-factors validation remain necessary.

items.title: A multi-source EO Framework for assessing permafrost thawing impact on land degradation in the Arctic region
items.abstract: EarthTrends is a multi-source Earth Observation framework developed to assess the impact of permafrost thaw on land degradation across the Arctic. Rapid warming is accelerating processes such as thermokarst formation, vegetation change, slope instability, and risks to infrastructure, yet monitoring these dynamics requires integrating heterogeneous satellite datasets and analytical methods. EarthTrends addresses this challenge through a modular Python architecture that fuses long-term satellite archives (Landsat), Copernicus Sentinel data, MODIS time series, and high-resolution optical imagery with advanced statistical and artificial intelligence approaches. The framework quantifies ecosystem change using multi-sensor vegetation index time series analysed through linear regression, Mann–Kendall trend tests, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to detect non-linear dynamics and anomalies. Thermokarst features are automatically mapped from high-resolution imagery using a U-Net deep learning segmentation model. Land degradation susceptibility is further evaluated by modelling soil freeze–thaw cycles as proxies for slope instability and landslide potential. Environmental indicators are intersected with socio-economic datasets to estimate impacts on settlements and infrastructure. Preliminary results show that the thermokarst detection component is operational and capable of identifying surface subsidence features, while freeze–thaw analyses reveal anomalies linked to areas of increased degradation risk. Vegetation trends highlight spatially heterogeneous ecosystem responses to warming across the Arctic. Overall, EarthTrends demonstrates the feasibility of an integrated, scalable framework for monitoring permafrost-driven environmental change and its societal implications. The system is intended for pan-Arctic application and will be released as an open-source tool to support research, monitoring, and decision-making related to climate-induced land degradation.

items.title: A Pipeline for Mapping FDA-Approved Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAATs) to NCBI Taxonomy
items.abstract: Background The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) catalogs in vitro diagnostics, including Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAATs), using unstructured clinical terminology. Because these regulatory labels often diverge from standardized biological taxonomy, they obstruct automated post-market surveillance and computational integration, particularly for in silico inclusivity audits against emerging pathogen variants. This study aimed to build a reproducible computational pipeline that translates historical FDA microbial NAAT records into machine-actionable biological identifiers. Methods Synthesizing clinical diagnostic logic, taxonomic normalization rules, and modern text mining, the workflow utilized the R ellmer package to interface with a Large Language Model (LLM) for Technology Classification, successfully isolating true NAATs from 510(k) summary documents. Subsequent algorithmic partitioning and LLM-driven Named Entity Recognition (NER) mapped complex syndromic labels and clinical abbreviations to National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Taxonomy Identifiers (TaxIDs). Results While only 20% of initial FDA records mapped directly to NCBI Taxonomy, the automated deconvolution of syndromic panels and NER extraction expanded and normalized the dataset. The pipeline successfully generated FDA510kPathogens, a highly granular master repository containing 457 unique pathogen-to-submission entries formally linked to enriched NCBI TaxIDs and metadata. Conclusions By programmatically translating human-readable regulatory metadata into machine-actionable biological descriptors, this open-source digital infrastructure resolves a critical informatics bottleneck. This provides diagnostic laboratories and developers with the foundational data necessary to conduct continuous, automated validation of molecular assays.

items.title: A PRELIMINARY STUDY OF AI-BASED PSYCHIATRIC COUNSELLING TO MANAGE EMPLOYEES STRESS AND TO ASSESS WORKPLACE MENTAL HEALTH BY THE END OF THIS DECADE (2030)
items.abstract: Background: Workplace stress, anxiety, burnout and psychological distress are important concerns affecting employee well-being and organisational performance. The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital mental health support offers opportunities for accessible and timely assistance, while raising concerns regarding privacy, informed consent, algorithmic bias, clinical safety, accountability and human oversight. This study aims to examine the potential role and responsible integration of AI-based psychiatric counselling for managing employee stress and supporting workplace mental health by 2030. Materials and Methods: A mixed-methods research design will be used, combining quantitative survey data with qualitative interviews. The quantitative component will include approximately 350–450 employees, while the qualitative component will involve approximately 25–35 interviews with HR professionals, organisational leaders, EAP professionals and mental health practitioners. Data will assess perceived stress, anxiety, burnout, psychological safety, trust, confidentiality, privacy concerns, AI counselling acceptance and willingness to use AI-based mental health support. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability testing, correlation, regression, t-tests, ANOVA and appropriate mediation or moderation analyses. Qualitative data will be analysed thematically. Results: The study is expected to identify factors influencing employee acceptance and trust in AI-based psychiatric counselling and to examine the role of privacy, human oversight, psychological safety and organisational support in its responsible adoption. Conclusion: AI-based psychiatric counselling may serve as a supportive component of workplace mental health systems, particularly for early support, psychoeducation, self-help and triage. However, it should complement rather than replace qualified mental health professionals. Responsible implementation will require privacy safeguards, informed consent, clinical oversight, transparency, fairness, accountability and clear referral pathways.

items.title: A RAG-enhanced multimodal large language model framework for culvert inspection
items.abstract: Despite their importance for maintaining infrastructure integrity, manual culvert inspections pose significant operational challenges for agencies such as the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) due to high labor demands, subjective assessments, and variability in evaluation outcomes. This study investigates the application of computer vision for automated culvert inspection, leveraging both supervised machine learning and emerging vision–language models. We proposed a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)–enhanced multimodal large language model (MLLM) framework that interprets culvert-condition imagery based on the culvert inspection manual. By embedding a small set of curated visual exemplars into a shared space, we enabled image-based retrieval to ground model reasoning alongside the full inspection manual. For the MLLM component, we selected three open-source models (Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3, LLaVA-OneVision) and one proprietary model (Gemini-3-Flash). We evaluated performance using precision, recall, and F1-score, alongside a practical “most-severe-label” decision rule to simulate maintenance prioritization. Results showed that the RAG-enhanced Gemini-3-Flash achieved the highest severity accuracy (91.16%), outperforming the supervised ConvNeXt multi-label baseline (84.54%) and other evaluated MLLMs. Overall, the findings suggest that RAG-enhanced Gemini-3-Flash can improve the reliability of severity-relevant decisions while reducing data-labeling requirements by approximately 99% (from thousands of training images to just 127 exemplars) and the GPU-intensive training burden, with the primary trade-offs being reliance on proprietary APIs and token-based inference costs.

items.title: A Relational Inquiry into AI Generativity: The Historical Formation of Judgment and Its Role in Value Recognition
items.abstract: This theoretical discussion paper examines how artificial intelligence participates in cognition, judgment, and generative activity through historically constituted relations among models, humans, other artificial agents, institutions, and environments. It distinguishes equal access to foundational technical capability from equality of situated performance, evaluative and generative judgment, practical opportunity, social recognition, and authority. A preliminary Generative Relational Theory (GRT) perspective treats historically conditioned AI configurations as candidates for relational reality where sufficiently stable causal efficacy can be established, while suspending claims about consciousness and ultimate ontological status. The analysis considers how interaction histories, conversational practices, memory, feedback, aesthetic preferences, and normative criteria may shape the realization of AI capabilities. It also investigates coordination conventions and rule-like practices among interacting AI agents, their uncertain normative authority, and the distinct processes through which generated contributions acquire recognition and institutional influence. Findings from existing experiments and field studies are interpreted within their task-specific limits, including evidence concerning heterogeneous productivity, creative diversity, contextual accommodation, and collective coordination. A comparative research program is proposed to distinguish historical causal contributions from prompt effects, unequal information, institutional selection, and other rival explanations. Relational differentiation may coexist with convergence or the reduction of existing disadvantages. The paper neither reports new experiments nor establishes a general law of AI-mediated inequality; questions of legitimacy and justice require normative arguments in addition to causal analysis.

items.title: A roadmap for modernizing vaccine safety assessment: Challenges and opportunities for new approach methodologies
items.abstract: Vaccines are administered to large populations of healthy individuals, including vulnerable groups, making an exceptionally rigorous safety profile a prerequisite for their approval and use. Nonclinical vaccine safety assessment has traditionally relied on standardized animal testing methodologies, which face increasing challenges: the ethical imperative to reduce animal use, the need for faster vaccine development, and the limitations of animal models in predicting human-specific immune responses. The advent of modern vaccine platforms such as mRNA technologies and viral-vector vaccines necessitates a re-evaluation of safety frameworks. This article explores emerging strat­egies to modernize vaccine safety assessment, integrating new approach methodologies (NAMs), including in vitro systems, artificial intelligence, and adverse outcome pathways (AOPs). Ethical refinements to animal husbandry practices, including group housing, humane endpoints, pain man­agement and scaled blood sampling volumes, are also discussed to align with the principles of the 3Rs (replacement, reduction, refinement). The adoption of molecular and omics-based techniques, along with innovative validation strategies, offers opportunities to improve predictive accuracy and mechanistic insight. The article highlights a strategic framework for implementing NAMs across the three stages at which animals are still used – early screening, late nonclinical development, and batch release – while ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements. Implementation must be careful enough to ensure that the use of NAMs in the safety evaluation of vaccines maintains or exceeds current safety assessment standards. By addressing scientific, ethical, and regulatory challenges, NAMs have the potential to transform vaccine safety assessment, enhancing human relevance and accelerating innovation in vaccine development. Plain language summaryThis article examines the evolving landscape of vaccine safety assessment, focusing on opportunities to modernize testing approaches through new approach methodologies (NAMs). Drawing on recent discussions with stakeholders across industry, academia, and regulatory bodies, we outline key chal­lenges and strategic pathways for implementing NAMs in vaccine development while maintaining robust safety standards. Special attention is given to emerging technologies, such as human-relevant test systems, artificial intelligence, and virtual control groups, to the replacement of animal-based potency, pyrogen and adventitious agent tests used for batch release, and to considerations for regu­latory acceptance and implementation strategies.

items.title: A scoping review of transformer and large language model approaches for word sense disambiguation in multilingual and low resource settings from 2019 to 2026
items.abstract: Abstract Background In natural language processing, word sense disambiguation (WSD) is still a significant difficulty, especially in low-resource, multilingual environments with few annotated resources. Contextual semantic representation and WSD performance have been enhanced by recent developments in transformer architectures and large language models (LLMs). However, there is still little evidence synthesis in multilingual and genuine low-resource situations, and research is still dispersed across architectures, datasets, and evaluation systems. Methods In order to map evidence on transformer and LLM-based Word Sense Disambiguation techniques published between 2019 and January 2026, this scoping study used the PRISMA-ScR methodology. Google Scholar database was searched for relevant literatures. Studies that used transformer or LLM-based techniques for WSD and reported evaluation criteria like accuracy or F1-score were considered eligible. A structured framework comprising model architectures, datasets, evaluation techniques, adaption strategies, and important discoveries was used to chart the data descriptively. Results Nine studies were included in the analysis. Gloss-aware transformers, poly-encoder architectures, multilingual transfer learning, morphologically aware fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adapters, and LLM-based reasoning were among the main topics. Model scale alone does not seem to have as much of an impact on WSD performance as architectural design and contextual modeling. Evidence for really low-resource languages was still scarce, though. Conclusion Transformer and LLM-based methods show immense potential for improving WSD in multilingual contexts. However, there are still gaps in robustness assessment, benchmark standardization, and the wider inclusion of low-resource languages that are underrepresented.

items.title: A Socio-Ecological and Evidence-Based Framework for Inclusive Elevator System Design in China
items.abstract: This study develops an evidence-based, context-sensitive framework for inclusive elevator system design in China. Drawing on the Capability Approach, the Biopsychosocial Model, inclusive design perspectives, and social ecology, it combines qualitative interviews and quantitative surveys to examine users’ capabilities, psychological processes, and social interactions across age groups and elevator contexts. The findings indicate that elevator experiences reflect interactions among physical and cognitive capabilities, psychological perceptions, and socially shared behaviors. Older adults showed greater mobility and sensory constraints, middle-aged users reported stronger hygiene and emergency-related concerns, and younger users showed greater sensitivity to efficiency and interpersonal pressure. Differences were also identified between residential and public elevators. The Function–Behavior–Structure framework was then used to translate these behavioral findings into prioritized design recommendations. The proposed approach supports targeted responses where user needs differ while maintaining standardized solutions for shared social norms, providing a transferable pathway for inclusive public infrastructure design.

items.title: A Two-Tier Blockchain Architecture for Verifiable Explainable-AI Audit Trails: Individual and Merkle-Batched Commitment of SHAP-Based Fraud-Detection Decisions
items.abstract: Machine learning systems that make automated decisions, including fraud flags, loan denials, and safety interlocks, typically generate an explanation (for example via SHAP) in the same trust domain as the model itself, leaving no independent proof that the explanation shown to an auditor is the one the model actually produced at decision time. This research presents and empirically evaluates a blockchain-anchored explainable-AI (XAI) audit-trail architecture that closes this gap by committing a canonical SHA-256 hash of each decision-and-explanation record to an Ethereum-compatible ledger, while keeping the full record, including the SHAP explanation, off-chain. The architecture is implemented end to end on a real fraud-detection pipeline consisting of a LightGBM classifier trained on the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection dataset (590,540 transactions), a SHAP TreeExplainer layer producing per-transaction feature attributions, a canonical JSON serialization and hashing procedure, and two complementary Solidity smart contracts: one committing each audit record individually, and the other committing batches of records via a Merkle root. Using 500 audit records, the schemes are benchmarked on an Ethereum-compatible network across batch sizes of 10 to 500 records and extended with synthetic hashes to 1,000, 2,500, and 5,000 records. Individual commitment registers a record in 6.3 to 17.4 ms at 139,300 gas per record. Merkle-root batching reduces on-chain gas consumption by 91.6% at 10 records to 99.98% at 5,000 records, with reduction factors rising from roughly 12-fold to nearly 5,982-fold. Tamper-detection trials correctly flagged altered records in 100% of cases. The work contributes a reproducible, empirically costed reference architecture for verifiable AI explanation integrity, and a direct, quantified comparison of two on-chain commitment strategies across three orders of magnitude of batch size that prior blockchain-XAI proposals have not benchmarked head to head.

items.title: A TYPOLOGY-INFORMED METHODOLOGICAL MODEL FOR BUILDING AN UZBEK–CHINESE PARALLEL CORPUS
items.abstract: Uzbek and Mandarin Chinese lie at opposite ends of the morphological spectrum: Uzbek is an agglutinative Turkic language with SOV order and a rich case system, whereas Chinese is an isolating Sino-Tibetan language with SVO order, function words and numeral classifiers, written without word boundaries. Our search did not identify a systematic, openly available Uzbek–Chinese parallel corpus; the only directly relevant study found builds a filtered, partly LLM-generated pseudo-parallel dataset from news crawls. This paper proposes a typology-informed methodological model for building such a corpus. It has five components: (1) a layered design separating a human-verified gold core, an automatic extension and a labelled synthetic layer, with provenance metadata; (2) asymmetric linguistic processing linked through Universal Dependencies; (3) multi-level alignment down to the morpheme, with correspondence-type labels; (4) a "unit–set of equivalents" lexical database; and (5) retrieval-augmented integration with large language models. A correspondence table and two author-composed sentence pairs show that most grammatical correspondences are not one-to-one. An evaluation protocol is specified for future empirical work.

items.abstract: This thesis examines the psychological nature, components, and causes of academic burnout among students. Academic burnout is interpreted as a consequence of an imbalance between academic demands and personal resources. The factors that play an important role in its prevention, including self-regulation, self-efficacy, social support, intrinsic motivation, and teacher–student relationships, are analyzed. Furthermore, the main directions of psychological and pedagogical prevention are systematized.

items.title: Acceptable Uses of GenAI: Post-Secondary Students’ Judgements
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping academic practice in higher education, yet evidence on how students evaluate its acceptable uses remains limited. This study surveyed 988 post-secondary students across 39 countries, recruited through the Prolific online research platform, on the acceptability of GenAI use across 22 academic tasks using a binary Yes/No format. Using an interpretive framework grounded in normative boundary-setting, academic integrity values, and academic socialization, the analysis reveals differentiated acceptability patterns: Students endorse GenAI for instrumental and research-support tasks while maintaining normative boundaries around evaluative and judgement-intensive activities. Gender differences are minimal; level of study is the primary source of variation, with graduate students reporting higher acceptability for research- and professionally oriented uses. Respondents residing in Canada (n = 58) reported significantly lower acceptance of four text-focused tasks, including academic composition and summarization, than the non-Canadian cohort. Findings have implications for institutional policy, pedagogy, and academic integrity frameworks.

items.title: ACCESSIBILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF DIGITAL LEARNING RESOURCES FOR STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES IN INDIAN SCHOOLS
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Digital Learning Resources (DLRs) has fundamentally transformed the pedagogical landscape globally. However, for students with disabilities in Indian school settings, digital transformation presents a dual reality of unprecedented educational opportunity and severe systemic exclusion. This doctoral study investigates the physical, pedagogical, and technological accessibility of digital learning platforms and evaluates their empirical effectiveness on learning outcomes, cognitive engagement, and social inclusion for students with diverse disabilities across primary and secondary schools in India.Employing a mixed-methods sequential explanatory research design (N=450), data were systematically collected across urban, semi-urban, and rural school establishments in West Bengal, Maharashtra, and the National Capital Region (NCR). Quantitative assessments involved Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA) technical compliance audits of flagship state and national digital portals (including DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and SWAYAM Prabha) alongside standardized Likert-scale surveys measuring technological self-efficacy, user satisfaction, and learning gains.

items.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions and guides current-task actor learning, while prior behavior is preserved by distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes. Fixed visual features keep the inherited learner and its replay compatible with base-policy updates. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and significantly reduces real-robot training time by 31.0\% to 68.5\%.
